label.fr: Marque de luxe et haut de gamme

expects.rule: The first screen states the brand and one idea in a short line, with imagery of the product or its making; the visitor should not need to scroll to know what the house sells.
Product and craft photography is large, consistent in lighting and crop, and sharp on high-density phone screens.

Where products are sold online, price, edition size or availability and delivery terms are stated plainly; luxury shoppers still leave over distrust (19% of abandoned carts cite distrust with card details, per Baymard).
A route to a boutique, appointment or advisor is one click from any page (Find a Boutique, Book an appointment).
Currency and language choices are offered in the header; copy exists in the languages of the main markets.
Motion triggered by scrolling or interaction can be turned off or follows the reduced-motion setting (WCAG 2.3.3, level AAA); keep a skip link and do not hide content behind animation.
Legal, shipping and returns information stays reachable and readable even when the visual style is minimal.

traits: Of the 6 seen on screenshots, 5 put one photograph, video or two split photographs across the whole first screen (Spyker, ESR, Unimatic, Deadly Ponies, AgnesToth); Forge showed a black loader.
4 of 6 had a cookie box or pop-up over the picture on load (Spyker, Unimatic, Deadly Ponies, AgnesToth).
The first-screen headline is under 10 words on 4 of 6 (3 to 5 words on Spyker, ESR, AgnesToth); the rest is a link or a label.
All 6 use two typefaces, one of them condensed, serif or monospace for the display line and the nav; uppercase small type is used for links on 4.
Navigation is short: 3 to 6 text links on 4 of 6 (Unimatic, Deadly Ponies, AgnesToth, ESR); Spyker hides it behind an icon.
Cart control in the header of 4 of 6 (Spyker bag icon, Unimatic, Deadly Ponies, AgnesToth with a (0) count); a currency choice is shown on 2 (Deadly Ponies, AgnesToth).
Palette is black, white or one neutral, with the product supplying colour; no first screen uses gradients or a bright brand colour on the interface.
Two of the added sites (Cartier microsite, Odyssee) were read from page text only, so their measures are not counted here.

sites.name: Spyker Cars
sites.why: Full-screen close-up of a car's red leather interior under a small line and a four-word capitalised headline in condensed Futura, one white button (Discover the C8 Preliator XXV Coupe), menu icon left, logo centre, bag icon right; a cookie box covers the lower left. Swiss 721 for small text.

sites.name: Forge Automotive
sites.why: The screenshot caught a black loading screen: a small logo, a spaced-capital line about bespoke vehicles being built on distinction, desire and identity, and a progress bar. The page then runs a portrait photograph row (Lamborghini, Porsche, Defender). GeistSans with a serif display face.

sites.name: ESR Bespoke
sites.why: Dark video of a grey sports car in a city street under a large white 'Exceptional is our standard' (two lines), name and 'Automotive Group' across the top, five nav links stacked in a column, a small description in capitals, Unmute and Our story links. Two typefaces; no button.

sites.name: Unimatic
sites.why: Dark brown ground with four watches on white truffles, a pill nav (New in, Watches, Straps, Accessories, Our world, Find us), Search, Account, Wishlist and Cart pills in mono type, bold sans headline at the lower left; a cookie box covers the bottom. Hero on the Langhe collection.

sites.name: Deadly Ponies
sites.why: Split screen: a suede trainer left, a woven tote right, each with an underlined link; thin banner 'Complimentary express shipping worldwide', serif wordmark, Bags, Shoes, Accessories, EUR, bag icon; a pop-up about shipping outside New Zealand covers the middle.

sites.name: AgnesToth
sites.why: Blurred full-screen video of a green woven handbag; four nav links left, logo centre, Log in, Cart (0), EUR and an outlined Enquire button right; large serif headline 'House of Luxurious Embroidery' bottom left, partly hidden by a cookie box. Jost and FreightBig Pro.

sites.name: Cartier, Le Choeur des Pierres
sites.why: High-jewellery microsite: header with Contact us, Services, English/Francais toggle, Find a Boutique and a Discover menu of eight categories (High Jewellery to The Maison). The page's own text is mostly menus; the story is told with gemstones in WebGL. (not seen on a screenshot)

sites.name: Odyssee
sites.why: Medical aesthetics clinic in Sydney: close-up portrait, headline 'Medical aesthetics for timeless results', a button to booking, nav of Treatments, Concerns, About, Book Consultation; phone, email, address as text. Navy and off-white. No prices. (not seen on a screenshot)

avoid: Stock photography or generic renders that could belong to any brand.
A full-screen consent, newsletter or country pop-up that appears before any product is visible.
Scroll-jacking or heavy intro animation that delays access to navigation.
Gold gradients, serif fonts and thin hairlines used as decoration with no product behind them.
Discount banners and countdown timers that contradict the positioning of the house.
Text set in light grey on photographs, unreadable on phones.
Menus with more than eight top-level labels.

sources.name: Baymard Institute, Cart Abandonment Rate Statistics
